SF Playhouse presents Peter Pan Goes Wrong

By Allyson Aleksey · October 7, 2026 · 1 min read

San Francisco Playhouse is presenting Peter Pan Goes Wrong, a comedy about an amateur theater company attempting to stage Peter Pan while a series of mishaps threatens to derail the production.

Written by Henry Lewis, Henry Shields and Jonathan Sayer, the play follows the fictional Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society as its members take on J.M. Barrie’s classic story. The production features flying rigs, sword fights and a crocodile, along with forgotten lines, malfunctioning scenery and rivalries that spill onto the stage.

The play is by the creators of The Play That Goes Wrong, which similarly follows a fictional theater troupe whose production goes increasingly awry. Peter Pan Goes Wrong premiered in London in 2013 before later moving to the West End and Broadway.

Susi Damilano directs the San Francisco production. The cast includes Greg Ayers, Joe Ayers, Maggie Mason, Christian McCooey, Ezra Reaves, Renee Rogoff, Patrick Russell, Sophie Schulman, Terrance Austin Smith, Jomar Tagatac and Phaedra Tillery-Boughton, among others.

The production runs through November 28 at San Francisco Playhouse, 450 Post St. in San Francisco’s Union Square neighborhood. Performances are Tuesday through Sunday, with evening and matinee performances on select days. The show runs approximately two hours and five minutes, including a 15-minute intermission, and is recommended for ages 8 and older.

Tickets and information for Peter Pan Goes Wrong and additional shows and musicals are available at sfplayhouse.org/.
